label: Web Proxy
description: Reverse proxy for explicitly allowed local HTTP and WebSocket services.
summary: Review proxy reachability, edit the outbound allowlist, and probe every allowed target.

servicesEndpoint.description: Workbench enumerator of the proxy's own routes and every mount it serves. web_proxy is the proxy itself -- the one plugin that is never proxied.

mounts.description: Redirects /pycoplex to the standalone harness server (same routes as the embedded router, on its own port).
Redirects /coplex to the standalone swipl REST server (prolog/coplex_server.pl).
Redirects /coplex_stdpy to the standalone harness server (same routes as the embedded router, on its own port).
Redirects /emullm to the Workspace Emulation Router plugin.
Redirect /mailbox_chat to the mailbox_chat REST/WebSocket relay.
Redirects /ws_collab to the Workspace Collab plugin.

plugin-lifecycle.note: Has no standalone process of its own -- it only adds routes to whichever process embeds it, so it needs the workbench startup/shutdown phases but is not workspace-scoped. workbenchStartupAfter (apply_plugin_init) is the one 'everyone's turn is done' hook actually wired up today: it runs once every plugin has loaded and declared its plugin-init requests, and mounts each one -- this is how /ws_collab, /emullm, and /mailbox_chat get proxied without web_proxy knowing about those plugins in advance.

status.description: Live status: allowed targets, reachability probe results, request timeout.

plugin-api.note: Embedded-only, no server of its own -- there is nothing to restart/shutdown independently of the whole workbench API process (see workbenchShutdown in plugin-lifecycle).

files.description: Manifest holding the outbound allowlist, mounted redirects, and transport settings.

steps: Install the httpx and websockets packages into the repository .venv.
List every origin this proxy may reach under Allowed targets.
Probe the targets and confirm each one answers.
web_proxy is first-party workbench source, not a vendored plugin, so there is nothing to remove beyond deleting the mounts and allowed targets it holds on other plugins' behalf.
Remove any mounts left in this manifest's 'mounts' list once the plugins that requested them are gone.
